MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | DevOps & Platform Engineering
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral test environments and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines supporting three product teams and has improved pipeline speed and test reliability through parallelisation, caching and environment automation. Hands-on with Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, with personal experience building a k3s homelab and provisioning Hetzner VPS infrastructure with Terraform. Seeking to move into a DevOps or platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
CI/CD and containers: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm
Infrastructure as code and orchestration: Terraform (personal projects), Kubernetes (namespace-level work and personal k3s homelab), Argo CD, Ansible (basic)
Monitoring and data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL, SQL
Languages and testing: Python, Bash, Java (test code), pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Other: Linux, Git, AWS (EC2 and S3 basics through personal learning)

EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage; monthly CI runner costs decreased by approximately 30%.
- Built merge-request ephemeral environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and used CI results to build Grafana dashboards for flaky tests.
- Wrote internal documentation explaining how the CI system works, which is used in team onboarding.
- Mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs to run nightly regression tests.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented short-lived review environments deployed through GitLab CI and Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster, with end-to-end tests running against each environment.
- Automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines across three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and separated end-to-end testing into its own stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by approximately 30%.

Flaky Test Dashboard | Odrava Health | 2023
- Collected CI test results in PostgreSQL and created Grafana dashboards showing flaky tests by team.
- Helped teams identify and address frequent failures; the flaky test rate fell from 7% to below 1%.

EDUCATION
BEng Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | Studying; exam scheduled for January 2027

LANGUAGES
Polish (native), English (C1), German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into CI/CD, test infrastructure and platform-adjacent work. The strongest evidence is quantified and credible: pipeline duration reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The ephemeral-environment and homelab projects make the career transition concrete rather than aspirational. The document is professional, readable and appropriately transparent about personal projects, namespace-level Kubernetes access, basic AWS exposure and the CKA certification still being in progress. The main content limitation is not writing quality but role fit: the CV does not establish the deeper cloud architecture, networking, security or production operations experience requested for this contractor role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, plain text bullets, searchable technology names and strong keyword coverage for GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, AWS, Linux, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, Argo CD and Ansible. It should parse well in most ATS systems. AI screening is likely to recognize a strong adjacent match for CI/CD, infrastructure automation, observability and Kubernetes test environments, but a weaker exact match for the role because Terraform is explicitly limited to personal projects and the CV contains no Terragrunt, mTLS, network design or practical security terminology. This is a genuine experience gap, not a keyword-formatting problem, so unsupported terms should not be added merely to improve ATS matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows hands-on infrastructure-adjacent engineering through GitLab CI ownership, ephemeral environments, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, PostgreSQL, observability dashboards and personal Terraform/Hetzner work. It also demonstrates analytical thinking, ownership, documentation, mentoring and measurable improvement. AWS is shown at a basic personal-learning level, and Java is shown in test automation. The candidate's material indicates gaps in strong Terraform and Terragrunt, systems architecture/system design at the level expected for shaping a new cloud platform, networking including mTLS, practical security awareness, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/full-stack development and virtual-machine experience. The CV is therefore a convincing transition profile for junior-to-mid DevOps/platform roles, but only a partial match for this cloud infrastructure contractor position. Relevant culture signals that are already supported include ownership, collaboration across product teams, technical improvement, documentation and bringing QA/product colleagues into review environments.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the strongest role-relevant evidence more prominent by changing the second sentence to: "Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and has improved delivery speed and test reliability through parallelisation, dependency caching, ephemeral environments and infrastructure automation." Keep the existing sentence about namespace-level Kubernetes work and personal Terraform/Hetzner infrastructure so the scope remains truthful.

2. In the Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to foreground collaboration and operational ownership: "Built and maintain merge-request ephemeral environments with Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster; each environment includes the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, supports QA and product review, and is automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This uses evidence already present in the candidate portfolio and better connects the work to the job's stakeholder and platform-support requirements.

3. In the Technical Skills section, keep the explicit qualifiers but make the distinction between professional and personal experience easier to scan by changing the relevant entries to: "Infrastructure as code and orchestration: Terraform (personal projects), Kubernetes (namespace-level professional work; personal k3s homelab), Argo CD, Ansible (basic)" and "Cloud: AWS (EC2 and S3 basics through personal learning), Hetzner VPS (personal Terraform project)." This prevents recruiters or ATS-assisted reviewers from interpreting Terraform or AWS as production commercial experience.

- “Helped teams identify and address frequent failures”

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with a clear DevOps transition narrative, relevant metrics, and credible project detail. The strongest evidence includes reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, reducing flaky tests from 7% to below 1%, owning CI pipelines for three teams, and building ephemeral Kubernetes environments. The structure is easy to scan and appropriately distinguishes professional, personal, and project experience. The main content limitation is that it presents a QA/test-infrastructure profile more strongly than a cloud infrastructure profile, and it does not explicitly frame the candidate's experience in terms of infrastructure engineering, system design, networking, or security where the available evidence supports only partial alignment.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, readable dates, and ATS-friendly keyword groupings. It contains useful terms such as GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Prometheus, Grafana, Linux, AWS, and PostgreSQL. ATS and AI screening probability is moderate rather than high for this specific role: the document will likely be recognized as relevant to DevOps and platform engineering, but rankings may be reduced by the absence of Terragrunt, mTLS, networking, system design, and explicit infrastructure-operation terminology. The document correctly qualifies personal, basic, namespace-level, and in-progress experience, which protects credibility. Do not add unsupported keywords merely to improve matching.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows meaningful alignment with hands-on infrastructure work, CI/CD, containers, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, Linux, analytical improvement, documentation, and technical ownership. It also shows AWS exposure at a basic personal-learning level, which is relevant but not equivalent to professional AWS operation. The major role-alignment gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, cloud environment design and operation at production scale, systems architecture/system design, mTLS and broader networking, practical security ownership, and IoT or remote-device integration. The candidate's material does not establish those capabilities, so they should not be added through wording. The CV does provide adjacent evidence for stakeholder support through QA/product review environments, onboarding documentation, ownership across three teams, and mentoring. The candidate also has Java test-code experience, but the material does not show backend or full-stack development.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary, change the opening and positioning so the CV more directly uses the role's supported terminology without overstating scope. For example: "QA automation engineer transitioning into infrastructure engineering, with 7 years of experience and the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, ephemeral test environments, build tooling and Kubernetes-based delivery workflows." Keep the existing qualification that Kubernetes work is namespace-level and that Terraform/cloud work is personal where relevant.

2. In the Professional Summary, add the supported stakeholder and communication evidence after the delivery-impact sentence: "Owns CI delivery workflows for three product teams, supports QA and product review through ephemeral environments, and writes onboarding documentation explaining CI operations." This makes the existing evidence more relevant to the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along without claiming formal cross-functional leadership.

3. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Infrastructure as code and orchestration" to "Infrastructure as Code and Container Orchestration" and format the qualifications more explicitly: "Terraform (personal Hetzner project), Kubernetes (namespace-level professional work; personal k3s homelab), Argo CD, Ansible (basic)." This preserves the current truth while preventing automated screening or recruiters from interpreting Terraform or Kubernetes as broad production-platform ownership.

4. In the Technical Skills section, change "Cloud: AWS (EC2 and S3 basics through personal learning), Hetzner VPS (personal Terraform project)" to "Cloud and VPS: AWS (EC2 and S3 basics through personal learning); Hetzner VPS (personal Terraform project)." This improves keyword parsing and clearly distinguishes learning/project exposure from professional cloud operations.

5. In the Selected Projects section under "Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps," explicitly include the supported security and networking terms: change the final bullet to "Set up Traefik ingress and cert-manager for SSL/TLS certificate management; provisioned a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform and used Ansible at a basic level." Do not add mTLS, network design, or security claims that are not supported by the candidate information.

6. In the Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise the ephemeral-environment bullet to foreground the infrastructure workflow and stakeholder outcome: "Built and maintained merge-request ephemeral environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster; each environment included the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, enabled QA and product review before merge, and was automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This is more closely aligned with the job's platform-operation language and uses evidence already present in the portfolio.

7. In the Experience section under Odrava Health Software, change "Wrote internal documentation explaining how the CI system works, which is used in team onboarding" to "Authored and maintained internal CI operations documentation used for team onboarding, improving the accessibility and repeatability of CI workflows." This strengthens the communication evidence without inventing a quantified outcome.

MINOR ATS / PRECISION IMPROVEMENTS
8. In the Certifications and Professional Development section, change the CKA line to "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — In progress; exam scheduled for January 2027." This keeps the qualification unmistakably unearned until the exam is passed and gives ATS a standard abbreviation.

9. In the Technical Skills section, change "Kubernetes (namespace-level professional work; personal k3s homelab)" to "Kubernetes / k3s (namespace-level professional work; three-node personal k3s homelab)." This adds a supported implementation detail and improves matching for Kubernetes operations without implying cluster administration in the professional role.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, quantified, and professionally written. It presents a credible transition from QA automation into DevOps/platform engineering, with strong evidence in CI/CD, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes usage, observability, and automation. The strongest content is the measurable impact: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by approximately 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The main content weakness is that the CV sometimes presents the candidate as a more experienced infrastructure engineer than the original information supports. The current role title is especially problematic because the original information identifies the official role as QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure), while the CV states DevOps Engineer. The document also does not clearly distinguish professional infrastructure experience from personal projects in every relevant area, particularly Terraform, AWS, and Kubernetes. The repeated project entries duplicate several experience bullets, but the duplication is still useful for demonstrating relevant project evidence.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly overall: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological formatting, plain text, recognizable technology names, and measurable achievements. Keywords such as GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, AWS, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, PostgreSQL, Python, and Bash are present. The headline and summary also contain DevOps, platform engineering, CI/CD, infrastructure automation, and ephemeral environments. However, the CV does not contain supported evidence for several important job keywords, including Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, certificate management as a security responsibility, and virtual machines. These should not be added unless the candidate has genuinely used them. ATS and recruiter interpretation would improve if professional and personal experience were labelled more explicitly and if the official job title were used rather than an inflated title. The CKA status is correctly presented as studying, not as an earned certification.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a credible partial match for the role. It shows hands-on infrastructure-adjacent engineering through GitLab CI ownership, Docker, Helm, namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, ephemeral environments, observability, and automation. It also shows AWS basics, Terraform through a personal Hetzner project, Linux, TLS-related homelab work through cert-manager, technical documentation, mentoring, and analytical improvement of CI performance and test reliability. These are relevant foundations for a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform role. The largest alignment gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud environment design and operation, mTLS, broader networking, practical security ownership, formal system architecture/design, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend/full-stack development. The CV should not imply ownership of the shared Kubernetes cluster or production cloud infrastructure because the candidate's notes state that the platform team operates the cluster and the candidate has namespace-level access. The candidate's experience leading technical topics is partially evidenced through CI ownership, documentation, and mentoring, but it is not yet equivalent to leading cross-team architecture proposals or stakeholder alignment in the way the ad describes. The role's AWS preference is only partially met because AWS exposure is limited to personal learning and EC2/S3 basics.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Experience section, change the current title “DevOps Engineer | Odrava Health Software” to the truthful official title “QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software.” If desired, add “DevOps / Platform Engineering Focus” after the title, but do not present DevOps Engineer as the formal employment title. This prevents the CV from overstating the candidate's official role while preserving the relevance of the work.

CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, revise wording that could imply broad infrastructure ownership. Replace “has improved delivery speed and test reliability through parallelisation, dependency caching, ephemeral environments and infrastructure automation” with wording that accurately describes the scope, such as: “has improved delivery speed and test reliability through CI/CD optimisation, dependency caching, ephemeral test environments and automation.” Keep the existing clarification that Kubernetes work is namespace-level and that Terraform is based on personal projects.

CRITICAL — In the Technical Skills section, make the experience status explicit for infrastructure tools. Change “Terraform (personal projects)” to “Terraform (personal Hetzner project)” and change the AWS entry to “AWS (personal learning: EC2 and S3 basics).” Keep “Kubernetes (namespace-level professional work; personal k3s homelab)” because this accurately limits the professional scope. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, virtual machines, or broader cloud-production claims because they are not supported by the candidate information.

MINOR — In the Experience section under Odrava Health Software, add the supported leadership and communication evidence currently omitted from the CV. Add bullets such as: “Wrote internal documentation explaining the CI system; the documentation is used for team onboarding.” and “Mentored two QA interns in 2023.” These bullets support the job's requirements for clear communication, ownership, and leading technical topics without overstating formal technical leadership.

MINOR — In the Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments project, retain the accurate scope phrase “to a shared Kubernetes cluster” and avoid wording that suggests cluster administration. Add the stakeholder outcome already supported by the candidate information: “Provided QA and product teams with short-lived environments for feature review before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment.” This better connects the technical work to collaboration and stakeholder enablement.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, quantified, and professionally written. It presents strong evidence of CI/CD improvement, ephemeral environments, test infrastructure, Kubernetes namespace-level work, monitoring, and automation. The progression from QA automation toward DevOps is clear. The strongest content is the measurable pipeline improvement from 38 to 14 minutes, the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%, and the scope of supporting three teams and approximately 25 developers. Main weaknesses are that the document is targeted at a relatively infrastructure-heavy contractor role while most professional experience remains test infrastructure, several target capabilities are only represented through personal projects, and the selected-projects section repeats information already stated in the experience section. The duplicated bullet under “Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments” is also a noticeable editing defect.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional headings, reverse-chronological experience, standard text formatting, and searchable technology keywords, so it should parse well in most ATS systems. It includes useful terms such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, AWS, Linux, PostgreSQL, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, TLS, Docker, Python, and Java. However, the title “DevOps Engineer” may be interpreted as an official employment title rather than a target-position label, despite the original employment information identifying the role as QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure). The CV also does not contain the exact terms “Terragrunt,” “mTLS,” “mutual TLS,” “network design,” “certificate management,” or “system design,” but these should not be added because the candidate information does not substantiate them. ATS keyword coverage is therefore good for CI/CD and test-platform engineering, but naturally limited for the core cloud infrastructure requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a credible adjacent match for CI/CD platform work, containerised environments, Kubernetes-based deployments, observability, Terraform experimentation, Linux, analytical problem solving, and technical documentation. It also supports stakeholder-facing delivery: the environments are used by QA and product teams, and the CI documentation is used for onboarding. The main alignment gaps are genuine candidate-profile gaps rather than writing defects: the candidate does not demonstrate strong Terraform or Terragrunt, production cloud environment design and operation, mTLS, broader networking, practical security ownership, IoT or remote-device integration, or backend/full-stack development. AWS is shown only through personal learning, while Linux is shown and virtual-machine experience is not. The CV should position the candidate truthfully as an infrastructure-oriented QA/DevOps engineer with hands-on delivery experience, not as an established cloud infrastructure architect. The role's contractor scope and expectation of leading train-to-cloud architecture are materially more senior and specialized than the documented experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Experience section, change the current title “DevOps Engineer | Odrava Health Software” to the accurate official title “QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software,” and optionally add “DevOps / platform-focused responsibilities” after it. Do not present “DevOps Engineer” as the formal employment title because the original candidate information identifies the role as QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure).

CRITICAL — In the Selected Projects section under “Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments,” remove the repeated bullet “Provided QA and product teams with short-lived environments for feature review before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment.” Keep the more specific version already covered by the surrounding bullets so the project has no duplication.

HIGH PRIORITY — In the Professional Summary, qualify the infrastructure scope more precisely. Replace “Hands-on with Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments” with wording such as “Hands-on with Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments for ephemeral test environments, plus personal experience building a k3s homelab and provisioning Hetzner VPS infrastructure with Terraform.” This preserves the strong match while clearly distinguishing professional namespace-level work from personal infrastructure work.

HIGH PRIORITY — In the Professional Summary or a concise “Selected Impact” line, make the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence more explicit using only documented facts. For example: “Owns CI pipelines used by three product teams, provides review environments to QA and product teams, and authored the CI documentation used for onboarding.” This better supports the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along without claiming formal architecture leadership.

MINOR — In the Technical Skills section, change “AWS (personal learning: EC2 and S3 basics)” to “AWS (personal learning: EC2 and S3 basics)” only if retaining the cloud category, but keep the personal-learning qualifier visible. Likewise retain “Terraform (personal Hetzner project)” and “Kubernetes (namespace-level professional work; personal k3s homelab)” so ATS keywords are present without overstating production experience.

MINOR — In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, consider adding the documented onboarding and mentoring evidence as separate bullets: “Authored internal documentation explaining the CI system, used for team onboarding.” and “Mentored two QA interns in 2023.” These strengthen communication, knowledge sharing, and technical leadership alignment.
critique.critical_issues:
The current title “DevOps Engineer” is potentially misleading when used as the formal Odrava Health Software job title. The original candidate information identifies the role as “QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure),” while the candidate only requested changing it because the responsibilities are DevOps-adjacent. Presenting the changed title without qualification could be viewed as an inaccurate employment-history claim. Fix by restoring the official title and adding a truthful responsibility qualifier such as “DevOps / platform-focused responsibilities.”

The “Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments” project contains a duplicated bullet describing QA and product review environments. This is a document-quality defect and should be removed.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with a clear DevOps/platform-engineering direction despite the candidate's formal QA title. The summary establishes relevant experience, scope, tools, and measurable outcomes. The experience section uses strong evidence, including pipeline time reduction from 38 to 14 minutes, a 30% runner-cost reduction, approximately 900 tests, and flaky-test reduction from 7% to below 1%. The selected-projects section adds useful infrastructure evidence and makes the career transition credible. The CV is also transparent about personal versus professional experience, which strengthens credibility. Minor concerns are that the document is somewhat repetitive between Experience and Selected Projects, and some role-relevant capabilities such as stakeholder leadership, system design, and security are only implicit or not evidenced.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, readable text formatting, standard date and job-title structures, and strong keywords including GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, AWS, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS, and infrastructure as code. The explicit labels for personal, professional, and basic experience reduce the risk of misleading screening. AI screening probability is high for junior-to-mid DevOps, platform engineering, CI/CD infrastructure, and test-infrastructure roles, but moderate for this exact contractor role because the CV does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mTLS, production AWS infrastructure, or broad cloud operations. The use of symbols such as “|”, “->”, and “~” is unlikely to cause material parsing problems, although plain wording would be marginally safer.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with hands-on infrastructure engineering around CI/CD, containerized environments, Kubernetes namespaces, Helm, Terraform-based personal infrastructure, observability, Linux, analytical troubleshooting, and clear technical documentation. The CV also demonstrates ownership across three teams and collaboration with QA and product stakeholders through review environments and onboarding documentation. However, the candidate's material shows important role-level gaps: no Terragrunt, no mTLS experience, no explicit practical security work, no production AWS infrastructure experience, no IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, and no backend/full-stack development background. Terraform experience is primarily personal rather than production cloud infrastructure, and Kubernetes access is namespace-level rather than cluster administration. These are candidate-background gaps rather than defects that can be solved through rewriting. The profile is therefore a credible adjacent match, but not a strong match for the advertisement's full cloud-connectivity and secure fleet-infrastructure scope.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the stakeholder-leadership evidence more explicit without overstating authority. For example, change “Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams, provides review environments to QA and product teams” to “Owns GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams and delivers review environments used by QA and product teams to evaluate changes before merge.”
2. In the Experience section under Odrava Health Software, combine or cross-reference the overlapping Selected Projects evidence so the CV is less repetitive. Keep the detailed project entries, but shorten the corresponding repeated bullets in Experience or retain only the highest-impact result there. Do not remove the measurable results.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change “Terraform (personal Hetzner project)” to “Terraform (personal Hetzner VPS infrastructure)” and change “Kubernetes (namespace-level professional work; personal k3s homelab)” to “Kubernetes (namespace-level professional work; personal k3s homelab; Helm deployments).” This makes the scope and evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to interpret.

For example, change “configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS” to “configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management.” This remains fully supported by the candidate information and avoids implying mTLS experience.
5. In the Certifications and Professional Development section, retain the “Studying; exam scheduled for January 2027” wording, but format it as “Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — In progress; exam scheduled January 2027” so it cannot be misread as an achieved certification.
